title: Promoting effect of sulfated zirconia on the activity of Au catalysts for formic acid dehydrogenation mediated by amino acids
content: ZrO2 and ZrO2-SO3H were used as supports for the preparation of Au-based catalysts for formic acid dehydrogenation. The sulfated zirconium oxide drives the Au dispersion, favouring the formation of small metal nanoparticles and thereby promoting the activity of the resulting catalysts. Two catalyst preparation methods were investigated: incipient-wetness and deposition–precipitation. Deposition–precipitation provides a more finely and uniformly dispersed Au phase than incipient-wetness. The Au/ZrO2-SO3H catalyst prepared by deposition–precipitation reached a remarkable TOF of 1672 h−1 in the presence of triethylamine. A more detailed analysis, involving the calculation of TOFs normalized to surface, high-coordination-number and low-coordination-number Au sites, suggests a major contribution of edge and corner atoms to the catalytic activity. Furthermore, the replacement of triethylamine with non-toxic and accessible amino acids was also evaluated. In particular, glycine and l-arginine proved to be promising substitutes for conventional amines in formic acid dehydrogenation. In the presence of l-arginine, the Au/ZrO2-SO3H prepared by deposition–precipitation achieved a TOF of 865 h−1.
